sections.h2: What is Faribault like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Faribault is the county seat of Rice County, about 50 miles south of Minneapolis and Saint Paul, where the Straight River joins the Cannon River. The Census Bureau puts the July 2025 population at 25,040, a gain of 2.3 percent over the 2020 base. Interstate 35 runs along the western edge, with Minnesota Highways 3, 21 and 60 serving the city.

It is an older city by Minnesota standards: the town was founded in 1855 and incorporated in 1872, and the Alexander Faribault House from 1853 still stands near downtown. Sellers who can state their own house's age and the dates of major updates answer buyer questions faster.

sections.h2: How does Faribault's housing market compare with the Twin Cities suburbs?
sections.html:
The gap is large. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 give a median owner-occupied value of $241,500 in Faribault, compared with $473,900 in Eden Prairie and $646,300 in Edina. The ownership rate is 66.1 percent, median gross rent is $1,074 and median household income is $61,449.

  • Households: 8,938, averaging 2.48 people.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher: 17.6 percent of adults 25 and older.
  • Persons in poverty: 16.4 percent.
  • Mean travel time to work: 19.0 minutes, shorter than in Elk River.

A lower price point means repair costs weigh heavily. A roof or foundation repair takes a bigger share of the sale price here than in a suburb where the median house costs two or three times as much, which is why many owners price a repair against an as-is sale.

sections.h2: What jobs, schools and landmarks shape buyer demand?
sections.html:
Faribault's economy mixes retail, services and light manufacturing. The Faribault Woolen Mill, founded in 1865, closed in 2009 and reopened in 2011. The Tilt-A-Whirl amusement ride was invented in the city in 1926. SAGE Electrochromics, a window glass developer, is based here, and the Minnesota Correctional Facility sits on the former state hospital campus. Central Avenue, the main street, has a commercial block listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

Faribault Public Schools covers the whole city with an early childhood center, four elementary schools, a middle school, Faribault High School and an Area Learning Center. The Minnesota State Academies for the Deaf and for the Blind, Shattuck-Saint Mary's boarding school and a South Central College campus are also in town.

sections.h2: What do buyers find around a Faribault house?
sections.html:
The rivers and trails are the draw. The Sakatah Singing Hills State Trail starts at a trailhead on the old White Sands site and runs to Mankato, and Sakatah Lake State Park and Nerstrand-Big Woods State Park are nearby. Interstate 35 was finished around 1975, after which through traffic bypassed downtown, so Central Avenue has become a place for restored historic storefronts and the Paradise Center for the Arts.

Weather is part of the picture too. For 1991 to 2020, Wikipedia's table shows about 35.5 inches of precipitation and 43.3 inches of snow a year in Faribault, with record temperatures from minus 40 to 110 degrees Fahrenheit. Roof, gutter and basement condition therefore get a close look in any inspection, and receipts for recent work help your case.

sections.h2: What must I disclose in writing when selling in Faribault?
sections.html:
Minnesota's general rule is Section 513.55: known material facts, disclosed in good faith before you sign a purchase agreement. Add radon under Section 144.496, wells under Section 103I.235 and sewage under Section 115.55.

The well disclosure certificate matters at the county office. Rice County explains that when a transfer document requires a Certificate of Real Estate Value, well information is also required, and if there are no wells the document must say so. The filing fee for a well disclosure certificate is $54, and you can find out whether a certificate is already on file through the Minnesota Department of Health database or by calling 800-383-9808.

sections.h2: What are Faribault's rental rules if I want to hold the house instead?
sections.html:
All residential rental properties in Faribault must be registered, licensed and inspected. The city's July 2022 ordinance update ended the requirement for landlords to run criminal background checks, though it still recommends them, and it confirmed an occupancy limit of no less than two times the number of legal bedrooms plus one, with children under age two not counted.

Owners and managers of one or more rental units must hold Crime Free Multi-Housing Phase I certification before a rental license renews. The Building Code Division is at 208 First Avenue NW, phone 507-333-0359, and the rental division can be emailed at rental@ci.faribault.mn.us.

If the training, registration and inspection steps feel like too much for a house you inherited or moved out of, selling is the simpler path.

sections.h2: How are Rice County property taxes paid, and what happens at closing?
sections.html:
Rice County's Property Tax and Elections Office is in the Government Services Building at 320 Third Street NW in Faribault. Non-agricultural real property is due May 15 and October 15, agricultural real property May 15 and November 15, and mobile homes August 31 and November 15. Taxes of $100 or less for the year are due in full on the first date.

At recording, Rice County says to submit one check for recorder fees and a separate check for deed tax and mortgage registration tax, both payable to Rice County. The deed tax is processed by the Property Tax and Elections Department. State deed tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration under Section 287.21, and a Certificate of Real Estate Value is filed with the auditor under Section 272.115. The recorder's phone is 507-332-6114.

sections.h2: What options does a Faribault homeowner have?
sections.html:
• List with an agent: good for a house in sale-ready shape, with time to wait for a buyer and a loan.
  • Sell privately: you manage price, showings and the contract.
  • Sell for cash as is: often chosen for inherited houses, rentals with violations, or homes where repair bills would exceed what a retail buyer will pay.

Get written estimates for each, and ask what you would net after commissions, repairs and carrying costs through closing.

faqs.q: How much is a typical house worth in Faribault?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports a median owner-occupied value of $241,500 for 2020 to 2024. Your own house may sit well above or below that, depending on condition and location, so use it as a benchmark only.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Faribault rental that is behind on its license?
faqs.a: Yes. Contact the city's rental division at rental@ci.faribault.mn.us or 507-333-0359 to learn what is open, and disclose any known problems to the buyer. A new owner who rents the house will need to register and meet the city's inspection and certification rules.

faqs.q: Who handles recording a Faribault deed?
faqs.a: The Rice County Recorder at 507-332-6114 records deeds, and deed tax is handled by the Property Tax and Elections office. The county asks for separate checks for recorder fees and for deed tax, both payable to Rice County.

faqs.q: Do I need a well disclosure certificate?
faqs.a: If the property has a known well, yes. If you know of no wells, the deed can carry the statement that the seller does not know of any wells on the property. The county charges $54 to file a certificate.

faqs.q: When are Rice County taxes due?
faqs.a: May 15 and October 15 for non-agricultural real property. Agricultural property is due May 15 and November 15. Taxes of $100 or less for the year are due in full on May 15.
